title: Rigveda 5.60: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.60: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.60 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 379v-380v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.60.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 379v
translation.original_text:
1īḻe̍ a̱gniṁ svava̍sa̱ṁ namo̍bhir i̱ha pra̍sa̱tto vi ca̍yat kṛ̱taṁ na̍ḥ | rathai̍r iva̱ pra bha̍re vāja̱yadbhi̍ḥ pradakṣi̱ṇin ma̱rutā̱ṁ stoma̍m ṛdhyām ||
2ā ye ta̱sthuḥ pṛṣa̍tīṣu śru̱tāsu̍ su̱kheṣu̍ ru̱drā ma̱ruto̱ rathe̍ṣu | vanā̍ cid ugrā jihate̱ ni vo̍ bhi̱yā pṛ̍thi̱vī ci̍d rejate̱ parva̍taś cit ||
translation.text:
1I LAUD with reverence the gracious Agni: here may he sit and part our meed among us. As with spoil-seeking cars I bring oblation: turned rightward I will swell the Marut's, praise-song.
2The Maruts, yea, the Rudras, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and cars swift-moving,– Before you, fierce Ones! woods bow down in terror: Earth, even the mountain, trembles at your coming.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 379v (numbered 52v by the scribe) (OPenn image 380, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.59.7 ‹parvatasya nabhanūn acucyavuḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 380r (numbered 53r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.60.3 ‹krīḷatha marutaḥ ṛṣṭi-mantaḥ āpaḥ-iva›. Verses 5.60.1-2 end on this page.

2ā | ye | tasthuḥ | pṛṣatīṣu | śrutāsu | su-kheṣu | rudrāḥ | marutaḥ | ratheṣu | vanā | cit | ugrāḥ | jihate | ni | vaḥ | bhiyā | pṛthivī | cit | rejate | parvataḥ | cit

translation.original_ref: RV 5.60.3-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 380r
translation.original_text:
3parva̍taś ci̱n mahi̍ vṛ̱ddho bi̍bhāya di̱vaś ci̱t sānu̍ rejata sva̱ne va̍ḥ | yat krīḻa̍tha maruta ṛṣṭi̱manta̱ āpa̍ iva sa̱dhrya̍ñco dhavadhve ||
4va̱rā i̱ved rai̍va̱tāso̱ hira̍ṇyair a̱bhi sva̱dhābhi̍s ta̱nva̍ḥ pipiśre | śri̱ye śreyā̍ṁsas ta̱vaso̱ rathe̍ṣu sa̱trā mahā̍ṁsi cakrire ta̱nūṣu̍ ||
5a̱jye̱ṣṭhāso̱ aka̍niṣṭhāsa e̱te sam bhrāta̍ro vāvṛdhu̱ḥ saubha̍gāya | yuvā̍ pi̱tā svapā̍ ru̱dra e̍ṣāṁ su̱dughā̱ pṛśni̍ḥ su̱dinā̍ ma̱rudbhya̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
3Though vast and tall, the mountain is affrighted, the height of heaven is shaken at your roaring When, armed with lances, ye are sporting, Maruts, and rush along together like the waters.
4They, like young suitors, sons of wealthy houses, have with their golden natures decked their bodies. Strong on their cars, the lordly Ones, for glory, have set their splendours on their forms for ever.
5None being eldest, none among them youngest, as brothers they have grown to happy fortune. May their Sire Rudra, young and deft, and Pr̥iṣni pouring much milk, bring fair days to the Maruts.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.60.6-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 380v
translation.original_text:
6yad u̍tta̱me ma̍ruto madhya̱me vā̱ yad vā̍va̱me su̍bhagāso di̱vi ṣṭha | ato̍ no rudrā u̱ta vā̱ nv a1̱̍syāgne̍ vi̱ttād dha̱viṣo̱ yad yajā̍ma ||
7a̱gniś ca̱ yan ma̍ruto viśvavedaso di̱vo vaha̍dhva̱ utta̍rā̱d adhi̱ ṣṇubhi̍ḥ | te ma̍ndasā̱nā dhuna̍yo riśādaso vā̱maṁ dha̍tta̱ yaja̍mānāya sunva̱te ||
8agne̍ ma̱rudbhi̍ḥ śu̱bhaya̍dbhi̱r ṛkva̍bhi̱ḥ soma̍m piba mandasā̱no ga̍ṇa̱śribhi̍ḥ | pā̱va̱kebhi̍r viśvami̱nvebhi̍r ā̱yubhi̱r vaiśvā̍nara pra̱divā̍ ke̱tunā̍ sa̱jūḥ ||
translation.text:
6Whether, O blessed Maruts, ye be dwelling in highest, midmost, or in lowest heaven, Thence, O ye Rudras, and thou also, Agni, notice the sacrificial food we offer.
7O Maruts, Lords of all, when Agni and when ye drive downward from sublimest heaven along the heights, Shakers of all, rejoicing, slayers of the foe, give riches to the Soma-pressing worshipper.
8O Agni, with the Maruts as they gleam and sing, gathered in troop, rejoicing drink the Soma juice; With these the living ones who cleanse and further all, joined with thy banner, O Vaiṣvânara, from of old.
